messages.author: 0c672754339d5578
messages.subject: large=internaldat and survey.weights
parts:
Hi Phil,

hope you are staying safe.

I get exactly the same number of iterations and likelihoods when using survey.weights and the large option:

#
internaldat <- mirt(data=dat,model=1,itemtype=psl_model,survey_weights=stu_weight,large=TRUE)
mod1 <- mirt(data = dat, model = 1,survey.weights=stu_weight, itemtype=psl_model,optimizer='L-BFGS-B',large=internaldat)
#
esti1 <- coef(mod1,simplify=TRUE)
#
internaldat <- mirt(data=dat,model=1,itemtype=psl_model,survey_weights=NULL,large=TRUE)
mod2 <- mirt(data = dat, model = 1,survey.weights=NULL, itemtype=psl_model,optimizer='L-BFGS-B',large=internaldat)
#

whereas the mirt() call does not even start iterations when using weights without the large option

best wishes

Matthias

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: large=internaldat and survey.weights
parts:
Hi Matthias,

Nice to hear from you, and thanks for the report. It looks like there's a typo in your code, since survey_weights is not a valid input (survey.weights, however, is). I get the expected behaviour without the typo:

#####
library(mirt)
dat <- Science

stu_weight <- sample(1:2, nrow(dat), TRUE)
stu_weight <- stu_weight / sum(stu_weight) * nrow(dat)

internaldat <- mirt(data=dat,model=1,survey.weights=stu_weight,large=TRUE)
mod0 <- mirt(data = dat, model = 1,survey.weights=stu_weight, optimizer='L-BFGS-B')
mod1 <- mirt(data = dat, model = 1,survey.weights=stu_weight, optimizer='L-BFGS-B',large=internaldat)
mod2 <- mirt(data = dat, model = 1, optimizer='L-BFGS-B',large=internaldat)

#####

HTH, and I hope that you are well and staying safe.

Phil
